title: PII Cryptography & Guardrails
tagline: Find personal data, swap it for deterministic tokens before the model sees it, unmask only what a role may see, and keep a tamper-evident log of every step.
why: Legal will not sign off on an LLM project until they know where customer PII goes. The answer that works: the model never sees raw PII. Values are swapped for keyed tokens on the way in, the output is checked on the way out, and only the roles that need a value get it back. Card numbers that must stay in legacy systems are encrypted without changing their format, and the audit log can prove nobody edited it.
covers: Detectors with validation: email, phone, SSN rules, cards (Luhn), IBAN (mod-97), IPv4, rule-based person names (titles + first-name list)
Deterministic tokens: HMAC-SHA256 per tenant key, value normalization, so the same customer gets the same token across documents
Proxy: pre-flight mask, post-flight block on raw PII, detection of tokens the model invented, unmask per role
Format-preserving encryption for digit strings (FF1-style Feistel), keep-last-4, separators kept
Hash-chained audit log with tamper, delete, reorder and truncation (anchored head) detection
gaps: Person-name NER is rule-based, not a trained model: plug in spaCy / Presidio for production recall
The FPE is FF1-shaped but uses HMAC, not AES; it is not NIST SP 800-38G validated
No key management: keys are inputs here; use a KMS / HSM and rotate per tenant
No real LLM call: model_output is given, so the demo runs offline

ops.label: Detect PII
ops.help: Validated detectors: the second card number fails Luhn and the order number is ignored, so neither is flagged.

input.text: Hi, this is Dr. Ana Souza. Reach me at ana.souza@clinic.org or 020 7946 0958. Pay to IBAN GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32. My SSN is 123-45-6789, card 5555 5555 5555 4444 (old card 5555 5555 5555 4445). Order 99812, server 10.20.1.7.

ops.label: Tokenize
ops.help: Each value becomes a keyed token. Change the tenant_key and every token changes; run it twice and they stay the same.

input.text: Customer Maria Lopez (maria.lopez@acme-foods.com, +1 (415) 555-0132) disputes a charge on card 4111 1111 1111 1111. Draft a reply and tell support what to check.

ops.label: Unmask proxy
ops.help: The model saw only tokens. A support agent gets the name, email and phone back, but the card stays hidden, and the model's invented token becomes [unknown]. Switch role to fraud_analyst or bi_dashboard.

input.prompt: Customer Maria Lopez (maria.lopez@acme-foods.com, +1 (415) 555-0132) disputes a charge on card 4111 1111 1111 1111. Draft a reply and tell support what to check.
input.model_output: Reply to <<EMAIL_9f53e85a75b9>>: Hi <<PERSON_7661f8b0f595>>, we are reviewing the charge on your card <<CARD_03ac6f4c9cc8>> and will call you at <<PHONE_e03673bb984a>> within 2 days. Support: check the last 3 transactions on <<CARD_03ac6f4c9cc8>> and the dispute history for <<EMAIL_9f53e85a75b9>>. Also notify <<EMAIL_000000000000>>.

ops.label: Block a leak
ops.help: The model output contains a raw email it never saw in the prompt. The proxy blocks the whole response.

input.prompt: Customer Maria Lopez (maria.lopez@acme-foods.com, +1 (415) 555-0132) disputes a charge on card 4111 1111 1111 1111. Draft a reply and tell support what to check.
input.model_output: Sure. I also cc'd jane.roe@gmail.com on this.

ops.label: FPE encrypt
ops.help: The card stays 16 digits with dashes and keeps its last 4, so it still fits the legacy column and the receipt UI.

ops.label: FPE decrypt
ops.help: Same key and tweak reverse it. A different tweak gives a different, wrong result.

ops.label: Verify audit log
ops.help: This is the proxy's audit log with one field edited after the fact. Verification names the entry. Undo the edit (entities back to 4) to see valid: true.
